<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/api/test_user_ssh_connection/{name}"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Attempts a key-only SSH authentication against the given git server with
the key the user's profile points at, and reports whether it was accepted.

Authenticates with exactly one identity and nothing else - the profile's
key, no ssh-agent, no ssh_config identity, no other key in the service
account's ~/.ssh - so a pass means *this* key works, which is the only
useful answer (see the -F and IdentitiesOnly options below for why that
takes more than passing -i). It runs `ssh -T` rather than `git ls-remote` on
purpose: the question is whether the host accepts the key, which a bare host
name can answer for every repository on it, and asking for a repository
would need one to exist and be readable.

Cannot hang and cannot prompt: BatchMode refuses every interactive prompt,
and ConnectTimeout bounds the TCP connect, with a hard subprocess timeout
behind both.

First contact with a host records its key (trust on first use) in the
user's own known_hosts, so a later test that finds a *different* key fails
loudly rather than shrugging - which is the interception case worth
catching, and the reason this doesn't simply disable host key checking.
